rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, three field studies (2004-2005) at Citra, FL with randomized complete block design. Q2: Table 3 and Section 3.4, sensor-based treatments SUR1 and SDI (applied only when VWC fell below set point in one of five daily windows) gave yields of 27.6 and 26.9 Mg/ha versus 20.5 for the once-daily timed SURtime; Section 3.3, the dry sensor threshold (SUR1, 2004) caused water stress and 12.4% lower yield, linking scheduling to crop water stress. Q4: Fig. 2 and Section 3.4, TDR-measured VWC (0-0.3 m) shows reduced fluctuations under sensor control; Fig. 1A compares cumulative irrigation with calculated ETc; Section 3.3 attributes SUR1 yield loss to irrigation below ETc after 60 DAS. Q8: Section 3.1, three frost events in 2005 reduced harvest events, growth and yield relative to 2004; Section 3.4, VWC oscillations in SDI were linked to salt-induced spikes in the capacitance probe readings after fertigation. Q9: Tables 2 and 3 report C.V. (%) for yield, IWUE and NUE; Fig. 1 bars show 1 S.E. of the mean.
rows.notes: Yield measured by one method (harvest weights), so no triangulation. One site, one soil type (sand), one crop; plot scale only. No condition for the yield effect is stated as a requirement, though authors note yield depended on soil water availability and the lower threshold caused stress.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field experiments on sandy soil. Q2: Section 3.4 and Fig. 1C, sensor-based SDI leached 1.7-2.4 kg N/ha versus 35-45 kg N/ha under timed SURtime; Abstract, sensor control reduced irrigation application and minimized N leaching. Q3: Section 2.2, nitrate leaching monitored by zero-tension drainage lysimeters (leachate volume and NO3-N) and independently by soil coring of nitrate at 0-0.3, 0.3-0.6, 0.6-0.9 m (Fig. 4), both showing N displacement under high-volume irrigation. Q4: Fig. 1B and Section 3.4, drainage volumes (62 mm for SUR2/SURtime vs 14 mm for SDI) and Fig. 2 TDR VWC fluctuations measured as the pathway from irrigation volume to leaching. Q7: Conclusions, sensor-based irrigation may give a consistent reduction of leaching when soil VWC is maintained within the field capacity threshold; Section 3.4, high irrigation volume (SUR2 at the 0.15 set point) still induced displacement and leaching. Q8: Section 3.1, frosts in 2005 reduced growth and yield; rainfall contribution to drainage assumed negligible under plastic mulch; Fig. 1 notes SUR1 drainage not monitored; Section 3.4, capacitance probe readings affected by salt spikes after fertigation. Q9: Fig. 1 bars represent 1 S.E. of the mean for cumulative leachate and NO3-N leaching; Section 3.3 reports soil nitrate concentrations with plus/minus values.
rows.notes: Leaching data only from one site/soil and plot scale.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field trials. Q4: Fig. 2 (TDR VWC), Fig. 1B (drainage) and Fig. 4 (soil nitrate displacement in profile) measured as the intermediate pathway by which high-volume timed irrigation displaced N and reduced dry matter and N accumulation. Q8: Section 3.1, 2005 frosts reduced harvest events, growth and yield; Section 3.4, probe readings affected by salt spikes after fertigation; several results given as data not shown. Q9: Table 3 reports C.V. (%) for yield, IWUE and NUE; Fig. 1 bars show 1 S.E.
